title: Cold rebuild: Split a master key
summary: Rebuild Split a master key from memory, no hints.

steps.title: Cold rebuild
body: Time to prove a piece stuck. You built **Split a master key** in *Key derivation: PBKDF2 and HKDF*. Now write it again from an
**empty editor**: no starter, no hints, no solution to peek at. The tests are exactly the ones you passed
Why: pulling something out of memory is what makes it stay there. Reading your old code feels like knowing
it; rebuilding it cold shows whether you do. If you get stuck, that is useful news: go back to the lesson,
then come back and try again tomorrow.
This check, plus the boss, is what proves the module.

steps.explain: Same inputs, same key (so you can decrypt later). A different salt gives an unrelated key, so two users with the same password get different keys.

steps.title: Rebuild Split a master key cold
prompt: Write `(byte[] Enc, byte[] Mac) DeriveKeys(byte[] master, string context)` returning two 32-byte keys from HKDF-SHA256 with no salt (`null`) and these info strings (UTF-8):

With the master key `00 01 02 ... 1f` and context `orders`, the encryption key starts `2206fd02`. Different contexts (say, `orders` and `invoices`) must give completely different keys, so a key leaked from one feature cannot touch another.
**From memory this time:** the editor starts empty and the tests are the ones you passed in the lesson.
Type the shape yourself, then fill it in:
(byte[] Enc, byte[] Mac) DeriveKeys(byte[] master, string context)
